title: What Animals Eat
objective: After this level you can explain herbivores, carnivores and omnivores.
summary: Herbivores eat mainly plants, carnivores mostly meat, omnivores both; teeth give it away. The giant panda is in the order Carnivora yet eats mostly bamboo.

cards.headline: The giant panda belongs to the meat-eaters' order. It eats bamboo.
cards.body: Up to 16 hours a day of it. So is a panda a carnivore or not? It depends on whether you're asking about its family tree or its dinner plate. Start with the plate.

items.label: Herbivore
points: Wide molars grind leaves and grass

items.label: Carnivore
points: Every cat, house cat to tiger, must eat meat

items.label: Omnivore
points: Can switch foods if one runs out

cards.headline: Read the teeth
cards.body: Teeth give a diet away. Wide molars grind leaves; long, sharp teeth grab and rip apart prey. A raccoon, an omnivore, carries both toolkits: sharp front teeth for ripping apart mice and large molars for chewing plants. Hand a biologist a skull and they're reading a menu.

cards.fact: A plant eater with a meat eater's gut
cards.context: The giant panda is a mammal in the order Carnivora, in the bear family, and its digestive system is more like a carnivore's. It can't digest cellulose, the main stuff of bamboo, so it pushes a lot through: 70 to 100 pounds a day. Remember Level 4's ranks? 'Carnivora' is the panda's order. What it eats makes it mostly a plant eater.

cards.headline: Diets: sorted
learned: The panda: order Carnivora, diet mostly bamboo

questions.prompt: What makes an animal an omnivore?

options.label: It regularly eats plants and animals
It eats only at night
options.rationale: Diet labels are about food, not timing.

questions.explanation: Omnivores, like bears, raccoons and humans, regularly eat both plants and animals.

questions.prompt: A skull has wide, grinding molars and no long, sharp teeth. What did the animal most likely eat?

options.label: Mostly meat
options.rationale: Meat eaters have long, sharp teeth.

options.label: Plants and animals equally
options.rationale: An omnivore like a raccoon also has sharp front teeth.

questions.explanation: Wide molars that grind leaves and grass are the mark of a herbivore.

questions.prompt: Level 4's ranks put the giant panda in the order Carnivora. What does its actual diet make it?

options.label: A strict carnivore, like its order
options.rationale: Its order is Carnivora, but it eats mostly bamboo.

options.label: An omnivore that hunts daily
options.rationale: Pandas eat mostly bamboo, not prey.

questions.explanation: The panda's order is Carnivora, but bamboo makes up most of its diet: rank and diet answer different questions.
